statement: For sigma(z)=z+0.001 tanh(z), iid Gaussian input and additive noise, |theta|<=1, batch1, eta in [0.99,1.01], the actual SGD maps contract on average; there is a unique invariant law with exact positive radial tail and unique exponent alpha in (1,2) solving E|1-eta A^2|^alpha=1.
limitations: Closes the registry concrete-example requirement only. Unbounded activation with bounded perturbation; streaming fresh data. Existing Brain results credited; no external peer review or priority certification.

statement: The same nonlinear teacher model at batch2 and eta in [1.1,1.2] has mean Lipschitz bound <0.8680084 and exact positive radial tail, alpha in (1,2), determined by E|1-eta Exp(1)|^alpha=1.
limitations: Only the stated batch-two rectangle; no global batch-monotonicity assertion.

statement: For the batch-one parameter rectangle, each one-sided stationary tail has constant C_abs/2>0, even at nonzero teacher, by the irreducible equal-slope sign matrix.
limitations: Equality of asymptotic constants does not imply stationary symmetry.

statement: The batch-one multiplier root alpha is C-infinity on (0.98,1.02), strictly decreasing there; rational derivative bounds and fixed-pair tail comparisons hold on [0.99,1.01].
limitations: Stationary-law conclusions are restricted to proved model ranges; no monotonicity of tail constants or entire distribution.

statement: For the zero-teacher batch-one model and deterministic start, subcritical moments converge, the critical moment grows linearly with slope alpha*m_alpha*C, and supercritical p moments divided by h(p)^n converge to a finite positive constant. Direct drift independently proves infinite stationary variance and exact second-moment exponential growth.
limitations: This supplement is proved for theta=0 and eta in [0.99,1.01]. General p assertions use the accepted stationary-tail theorem.

statement: Original Mirek Theorem1.8 and its additional positivity condition apply directly to the explicit nonzero-teacher model; with the chosen remainder envelope N=2(1+A^2+E^2), (E N^s / E|M|^s)^(1/s) tends to 2/eta as s tends to infinity.
limitations: An application of existing theory, not a newly discovered general theorem; does not invoke Mirek stable-sum Theorem1.15.
Conditional on documented Decimal/integer runtime arithmetic; optimized Python is rejected. The analytic proof does not depend on numerics.

statement: For continuous PSD kernels on compact Euclidean domains, including infinite rank, positive observation-noise variance, context length t<=n and bounded context labels |y_i|<=B, an explicit raw-input normalized-ReLU-attention transformer approximates the Gaussian noisy predictive mean and variance with uniform forward KL and explicit size bounds.
limitations: Kernel continuity, the stated architecture and real weights are assumptions. Does not close unrestricted T336 or prove optimizer convergence.

statement: The deterministic GP comparator admits explicit prior-average forward-KL ERM/generalization bounds with unbounded Gaussian target labels, context/output clipping, and finite-grid or full-box hypothesis classes.
limitations: Approximate empirical risk minimization is assumed to its stated error. No SGD training guarantee; W bounds fixed and trainable core/readout coefficients.

statement: Under convergence of second-moment coordinates, Adam on a positive definite diagonal quadratic with positive epsilon converges coordinatewise to zero or an alternating two-cycle. If at least one coordinate has nonzero limiting amplitude, active curvature converges to the stated frozen threshold; the top-curvature formula and epsilon obstructions have their stated conditional scopes.
limitations: Moment convergence, favorable random/standard initialization and quantitative burn-in remain unproved. Beta1=0.9 is stated before threshold38. No full T421 closure.
